stem: Which of the following statements about open fractures is correct?

options.text: Open fractures heal just as fast as closed fractures
Open fractures must go straight to operating theatre without fasting to be washed out to avoid infection
Antibiotics given in the first 3 hours from injury change the prognosis
Open fractures are always internally fixed as they are more unstable than closed fractures
Open fractures can be dressed, placed in plaster and referred to clinic on oral antibiotics

explanation: Early antibiotic administration is the key initial intervention in open fractures and improves outcome by reducing the risk of infection. The other options are incorrect because open fractures do not heal as quickly as closed fractures, do not require immediate theatre without appropriate preparation, are not always internally fixed, and should not be managed as simple outpatient plaster-and-oral-antibiotic cases.
rationale: Open fractures are emergencies because contamination and infection risk drive prognosis. Among the listed statements, the one reflecting evidence-based management is early antibiotic administration.

optionExplanations.A: Open fractures generally heal more slowly and have higher complication rates than closed fractures.
optionExplanations.B: Initial management includes urgent antibiotics, tetanus assessment, immobilisation and appropriate surgical planning; immediate unprepared theatre is not standard.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: early antibiotics after an open fracture improve prognosis by lowering infection risk.
optionExplanations.D: Fixation method depends on the fracture pattern and contamination; internal fixation is not always used.
optionExplanations.E: Open fractures need urgent assessment and usually hospital-based management, not simple clinic referral on oral antibiotics.
